```{=html}
  <div class="main">
    <section class="home-section" id="about" aria-labelledby="about-title">
      <h2 class="section__title" id="about-title">About</h2>
      <p>I am an Ezra Systems Postdoctoral Associate in Systems Engineering at Cornell University, where I work with <a href="https://www.peese.org/professor/">Professor Fengqi You</a> on AI for materials processing. I completed my Ph.D. at Shanghai Jiao Tong University in 2026 under <a href="https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37280547200">Professor Jingcheng Wang</a>.</p>
      <p>Physical intelligence is the ability of a learning system to model a physical system and to act on it. Both parts rest on the governing dynamics of the system. I train neural networks to solve those dynamics fast enough for design and control, and I measure how the error that remains in the learned solution changes the decision made with it.</p>
    </section>

    <section class="home-section" id="research" aria-labelledby="research-title">
      <h2 class="section__title" id="research-title">Research</h2>
```

```{=html}
      <ul class="directions">
        <li class="d-a"><strong>A. Physical systems in science and engineering.</strong> Science: the temperature and composition fields of a materials processing step, with Professor Fengqi You. Engineering: urban water demand, network pressure, day-ahead electricity price, and hot-strip rolling energy, from my Ph.D. with Professor Jingcheng Wang.</li>
        <li class="d-b"><strong>B. Solving the dynamics with neural networks.</strong> A neural operator maps initial conditions, boundary conditions, and forcing to the solution field in one forward pass. I train it so that its rollouts and sensitivities are accurate enough for a controller or an optimizer to use.</li>
        <li class="d-c"><strong>C. The model-to-decision gap.</strong> The difference between the decision computed from the learned model and the decision computed from the true dynamics. It is small over most of the state space and large near a critical point, and it is the training signal for B.</li>
      </ul>
      <p class="section__more"><a href="/research/">The full research program</a></p>
    </section>

      <div class="notes">
        <article class="note">
          <p class="note__meta"><time datetime="2026-09-07T11:40:00-04:00">7 September 2026, EDT (UTC−04:00)</time><span>Ithaca, New York</span></p>
          <h3 class="note__title"><a href="/thinking/#emergence-and-physical-intelligence">Emergence and physical intelligence</a></h3>
          <p>I do not expect physical intelligence to show the emergence reported for large language models. If a mechanism for wide transfer exists, it should come from structure rather than from parameter count, because the laws that govern a physical system have always turned out to be short.</p>
        </article>
      </div>
```
